import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = [14, 10]
plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 12

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Income distribution by education level (top-left)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
education_order = ['Basic', '2n Cycle', 'Graduation', 'Master', 'PhD']
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='Education', y='Income', order=education_order, ax=ax1, palette='viridis')
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Education Level')
ax1.set_ylabel('Income ($)')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Spending categories comparison (top-middle)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_means = df[spending_cols].mean()
spending_means.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax2, color=plt.cm.Set3(np.arange(len(spending_cols))))
ax2.set_title('Average Spending by Product Category', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Product Category')
ax2.set_ylabel('Average Amount Spent ($)')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Purchase channels distribution (top-right)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'NumDealsPurchases']
purchase_data = df[purchase_cols].sum()
colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1', '#96CEB4']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax3.pie(purchase_data, labels=purchase_cols, autopct='%1.1f%%', 
                                   colors=colors, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Purchase Distribution by Channel', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# 4. Customer age distribution (middle-left)
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']  # Assuming current year is 2024
age_bins = [18, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 100]
age_labels = ['18-29', '30-39', '40-49', '50-59', '60-69', '70+']
df['Age_Group'] = pd.cut(df['Age'], bins=age_bins, labels=age_labels, right=False)
age_counts = df['Age_Group'].value_counts().sort_index()
age_counts.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax4, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_title('Customer Age Distribution', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Age Group')
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Customers')
for i, v in enumerate(age_counts):
    ax4.text(i, v + 10, str(v), ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')

# 5. Household composition (middle-center)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
df['Total_Children'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
children_counts = df['Total_Children'].value_counts().sort_index()
children_counts.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax5, color=['#FF9999', '#66B3FF', '#99FF99', '#FFCC99'], edgecolor='black')
ax5.set_title('Household Composition (Number of Children)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Number of Children')
ax5.set_ylabel('Number of Households')
for i, v in enumerate(children_counts):
    ax5.text(i, v + 10, str(v), ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')

# 6. Campaign response rate (middle-right)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
campaign_names = ['Campaign 1', 'Campaign 2', 'Campaign 3', 'Campaign 4', 'Campaign 5', 'Latest Campaign']
response_rates = [(df[col].sum() / len(df) * 100) for col in campaign_cols]
bars = ax6.bar(campaign_names, response_rates, color=plt.cm.Paired(np.arange(len(campaign_names))))
ax6.set_title('Campaign Response Rates', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Campaign')
ax6.set_ylabel('Response Rate (%)')
ax6.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
for bar, rate in zip(bars, response_rates):
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax6.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 0.5,
             f'{rate:.1f}%', ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')

# 7. Correlation heatmap of spending and purchase behavior (bottom row, spanning all columns)
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :])
behavior_cols = spending_cols + ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 
                                 'NumDealsPurchases', 'NumWebVisitsMonth', 'Income', 'Recency']
corr_matrix = df[behavior_cols].corr()
mask = np.triu(np.ones_like(corr_matrix, dtype=bool))
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, mask=mask, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', 
            center=0, square=True, linewidths=1, cbar_kws={"shrink": 0.8}, ax=ax7)
ax7.set_title('Correlation Heatmap: Spending and Purchase Behavior', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax7.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax7.tick_params(axis='y', rotation=0)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor='white')
